## Findings
- claim-1: The source identifies \(J_{v_{r,s,t,n}}\) as the ideal of \(\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}\) generated by \(\{s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq(n-r)^r\}\). [source-2@L1365-L1375|claim=formal-document]
- claim-2: In the integral box-Schur/Pieri presentation, for \(p=c=1\), \(q=i+1\), \(r=j+1\), \(d=ij\), and \(\min(i,j)=3\), \[ M_{d+4}=\bigoplus_{\substack{i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq(i+1)^{j+1}\\|\mu|=d+4}}\mathbb Zs_\mu, \qquad (A_+M)_{d+4}=\sum_{\ell=1}^{4}h_\ell M_{d+4-\ell}. \] The requested target is established, subject to that ambient integral presentation.
## Strategy
Assume the integral box/Schur/LR/Pieri presentation: in \(A=\Lambda/I_{j+1,i+1}\), the in-box \(s_\lambda\) are a free \(\mathbb Z\)-basis and multiplication is box-truncated LR/Pieri. Then the ideal generated by \(s_\mu\) with \(i^j\subseteq\mu\) equals their \(\mathbb Z\)-span: LR-containment gives \(c_{\lambda\mu}^{\nu}\ne0\Rightarrow\mu\subseteq\nu\), and basis independence gives the direct sum. Hence the stated formula for \(M_{d+4}\).

Put
\[
P_{x,y}=s_{((i+1)^x,i^{j-x},y)},\qquad C_u=P_{u,4-u},
\]
omitting invalid boundary columns. Since \(\min(i,j)=3\), the degree-\(d+k\) bases for \(0\le k\le3\) are \(\{P_{x,k-x}:0\le x\le k\}\). The ten generator-Pieri rows in degree \(d+4\) are
\[
\begin{array}{c|c}
\ell&h_\ell P_{x,\,4-\ell-x}\quad(0\le x\le4-\ell)\\ \hline
4&h_4P_{0,0}\\
3&h_3P_{0,1},\ h_3P_{1,0}\\
2&h_2P_{0,2},\ h_2P_{1,1},\ h_2P_{2,0}\\
1&h_1P_{0,3},\ h_1P_{1,2},\ h_1P_{2,1},\ h_1P_{3,0}.
\end{array}
\]
Pieri gives, with unavailable \(C_u\) deleted,
\[
h_\ell P_{x,\,4-\ell-x}=C_x+C_{x+1}.
\]
Indeed, a horizontal strip can add either no box or one box in column \(i+1\); the remaining boxes extend the bottom part. Thus these ten rows are exactly the required degree-\(d+4\) product rows.

For an arbitrary homogeneous product \(am\in(A_+M)_{d+4}\), with \(\deg a=t>0\), use
\[
A_+=(h_1,\ldots,h_q),\qquad
a=\sum_{\ell=1}^{\min(q,t)}h_\ell b_\ell .
\]
Then
\[
am=\sum_\ell h_\ell(b_\ell m),\qquad
b_\ell m\in M_{d+4-\ell}.
\]
Since \(M_u=0\) for \(u<d\), all terms with \(\ell>4\) vanish. Therefore
\[
(A_+M)_{d+4}=\sum_{\ell=1}^{4}h_\ell M_{d+4-\ell},
\]
and the preceding ten rows directly span every homogeneous product.

Thus the requested target is established **conditional on** the integral box/Schur/LR/Pieri presentation.

## Gaps
The supplied source excerpt establishes the ideal-generating family, but not the integral in-box Schur basis or box-truncated LR/Pieri rule. Consequently, no unconditional proof of the displayed direct-sum presentation is supplied here.
